stories.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as ‘frontier models can’t be trusted’
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is warning companies that AI assistants built outside their control can be risky, like having someone access your computer systems without full supervision. They're telling workers to be careful and watch what these tools are doing.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use AI tools at your business, you should think about what information you're sharing with them, especially with new tools from smaller companies.

stories.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
stories.simple_summary: America is building more coal and natural gas power plants than it has in ten years, even though solar and wind power were growing faster before. Electricity use is climbing quickly because of new data centers, factories, and electric cars.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and policymakers thinking about energy. For your business or daily life, just know that the electricity grid is under strain, which could affect costs or reliability.

stories.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
stories.simple_summary: CoreWeave, a company that rents computer power for AI projects, is having money problems. Some investors are worried that too much investment money is flowing into AI companies that may not be sustainable.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies. There's nothing you need to do right now, though it signals that some AI projects may be burning money faster than they should.

stories.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is building new tools so developers can use AI on Amazon's computer chips instead of only on Nvidia chips. Right now Nvidia controls the tools most people use to build AI, and Amazon wants to change that.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech engineers and companies buying expensive computer equipment. If you're not building AI systems, this doesn't affect you yet.

stories.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
stories.simple_summary: Hackers got into an AI coding tool called OpenCode and stole access keys, which are like passwords that let you use AI services. They used stolen keys to run up charges on people's accounts.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use any AI coding tools, make sure your passwords are strong and watch your bills for unexpected charges. It's worth checking your accounts if you use this particular tool.

stories.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
stories.simple_summary: A company called Tolan that makes an AI friend to chat with has gotten more money to grow. It now has over 250,000 people using it regularly.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors. If you enjoy chatting with AI for company or advice, this just means the service will probably improve, but there's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago
stories.simple_summary: A person named Eugenia Kuyda created a new AI assistant called Wabi. She had the same basic idea twelve years ago but is now launching it as a free download that anyone can use.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in having a personal AI assistant, this is one option that's free to download. It's just one of many AI companion choices available now.

stories.title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips
stories.simple_summary: Tenstorrent, a company trying to compete with Nvidia by making computer chips for AI, raised 1.5 billion dollars. The company is now valued at 6.2 billion dollars.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and investors. It shows there's money flowing into companies that want to compete with Nvidia, but ordinary people won't feel the effects for a while.

stories.title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
stories.simple_summary: Some smart TV owners are using AI to remove all the ads, tracking software, and slow features from their televisions. They're trying to make their smart TVs work simpler and faster like older dumb TVs.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have a smart TV that's full of ads or runs slowly, you might eventually see tools that let you clean it up. Right now this is still quite technical, so it mainly appeals to people comfortable tinkering with their devices.

stories.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia is releasing new AI models that companies can run on their own computers instead of relying on Nvidia's online service. They're also focusing on AI helpers that work on personal computers with your private information.
stories.why_it_matters: For a business or person worried about privacy, this means more options to use AI without sending your data to the cloud. It's mostly useful for companies with technical teams who can set this up.

stories.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
stories.simple_summary: The governor of Illinois was interviewed about AI and talked about how it could help people live longer or become dangerous like nuclear weapons.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a political discussion about the future of AI. There's nothing you need to do based on what one politician thinks about AI.

stories.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
stories.simple_summary: A hacker used an army of AI agents to break into over 100 websites, including ones belonging to John Deere and SharkNinja. The AI agents did most of the work on their own without much human help.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that hackers are now using AI to attack companies more efficiently. If you own a business, make sure your passwords are strong and your computer systems are updated, just as you would have done before.
